name: Luchi and Alur Dom
instructions: 1. Knead maida with salt, a spoonful of ghee, and water to make a soft, smooth dough; let it rest for 30 minutes.
2. Boil potatoes, peel, and cut into cubes; shallow fry them with a pinch of turmeric until golden.
3. Heat mustard oil in a pan, temper with bay leaf and cumin seeds, then add ginger paste, turmeric, chili powder, and coriander powder.
4. Add the fried potatoes, salt, a pinch of sugar, and water to simmer until the gravy thickens.
5. Finish the curry with garam masala and a touch of ghee.
6. Roll the dough into small discs and deep-fry in hot oil until they puff up into golden Luchis.
description: Luchi and Alur Dom is a quintessential Bengali comfort food, often served during breakfast, festivals like Durga Puja, or special family gatherings. It is a beloved combination that perfectly balances the crisp, airy texture of the bread with the deep, savory notes of the potato curry.
